questions.stem: Why might a species that only reproduces asexually be at risk if the environment changes?

options.text: Because asexual reproduction is too slow
Because all offspring are genetically identical and may all be equally vulnerable
Because asexual organisms cannot move to new habitats
Because they produce too many offspring

questions.explanation: Since asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring, there is no variation. If the environment changes or a new disease appears, all individuals may be equally susceptible.
